Larry King once asked Bill Gates, one of the richest men alive, what his secret was. Gates said luck - being in the right place at the right time.

Kevin Trudeau points out Gates didn't stop there. Plenty of people were in that same room in those same years. What set Gates apart was vision: he saw what a computer could become when most people around him saw a toy.

A friend once tested Trudeau's own vision with a pack of matches: imagine this is an acorn, what do you see? Trudeau said a tree. The friend said, I see a forest.

Luck puts you in the room. Vision decides what you build there.

clips.caption:
Most people chasing a business idea start in the wrong place: with a product they already love.

Kevin Trudeau says that's backwards. The first question is never "what do I want to sell" - it's "what does a market already want?"

Campbell didn't invent a craving for soup. People already wanted it; they just didn't want to spend an hour making it from scratch. Campbell found the need, condensed the recipe, and let people add the water themselves.

Same old rule: if you want to get rich, don't invent a category. Build a better mousetrap for a market that already exists.

What market are you overlooking because you're attached to your own idea?

Before you can manifest anything, Kevin Trudeau says you have to answer one question honestly: what will you no longer tolerate?

Not a vague complaint - the exact thing. The debt, the relationship, the mood swings you can't control anymore.

Once you know what you don't want, you get precise about what you do want. See it, feel it as if you already have it, and hold that feeling for about 68 seconds. Then let go of needing it to happen.

Do that a few times a day and that's the entire formula in its basic form.

What's the one thing you're no longer willing to tolerate?

A newspaper ad running at zero orders. Kevin Trudeau says he worked through a mental block on it and felt something clear, like a ceiling lifting.

He reran the exact same ad, changed one word, and hundreds of dollars a day started landing in his mailbox. He made over a million dollars before he turned 18.

Right after that, a stranger stopped him at a deli and told him he should be on TV. That tip led to an infomercial that did $180 million in 18 months - his first royalty check alone was $250,000.

What's the one change you've been putting off?

clips.caption:
A client says eight words out loud without realizing what he just did.

Kevin Trudeau stops him mid-sentence: do you remember what you just said? He repeats it back - the man had just predicted, out loud, that he was going to fail.

No fear behind it, no old wound. Just a habit, worn into a groove like a scratch on an old record, repeating the same line every time he got close to a goal.

The fix isn't therapy. It's catching the moment it happens, saying cancel, cancel, and replacing it with a line that actually helps you.

clips.caption:
You can be doing everything right and still feel like you're dragging 800 pounds up a hill.

Kevin Trudeau calls it a counter intention: a hidden belief, often inherited from your own family, that works against every goal you set. You can't see it. You just feel the climb get harder for no reason, or a wind that only pushes back when you move forward.

Clear the belief and the resistance goes with it. You still have to walk to the goal - you just stop fighting yourself on the way there.

What's the invisible weight you've been carrying?
